rule.name: ActiveRecord Query with Raw Condition String
rule.rule_desc: The code constructs a query, selection, or ordering clause with values that may be externally controlled. Resolve whether those values enter syntax or bound data.
rule.vuln_desc: Attacker-controlled query syntax may change selected records, bypass intended filters, or modify stored data with the connection or provider’s privileges.
rule.developer: Bind data values using the query API’s parameter mechanism. Choose ordering columns and other identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce record-level authorization.
rule.reviewer: Confirm all where() conditions use array syntax or named parameter bindings without string concatenation. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Unsafe Mass Assignment via load() or setAttributes()
rule.rule_desc: Request-derived fields enter a bulk model-assignment operation. Resolve the model’s effective safe-attribute and validation rules.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker may set privilege, ownership, or other protected attributes and gain unauthorized access or alter trusted state if those fields are assignable.
rule.developer: Allowlist writable fields for each operation, exclude privilege and ownership attributes, and set protected values on the trusted server after authorization.
rule.reviewer: Verify model rules() define appropriate safe attributes and that sensitive fields are excluded from mass assignment. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: createCommand with Raw SQL String
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
rule.vuln_desc: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.
rule.reviewer: Confirm all createCommand() calls use parameterized queries. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
